cards.title: Positive sharp singular calibration and exact conformal reductions
cards.scientific_scope: Unchanged positive sharp J_r on real 2x2 matrices, r>0, periodic or zero-boundary W1,4 compatible tests.
cards.statement: The exact Gram/determinant calibration proves strict QC at every singular background and an explicit open full-rank cone for every r>0. At r1 it gives fourth-order margin 1/32 on singular backgrounds. At I and diag(1,-1), nonlinear acoustic-shear elimination has an attained unique convex inner optimum and an exact outer inequality equivalent to the corresponding conformal QC. A separate attained scalar-row divergence-free stress dual is equivalent at I. The universal outer inequalities and all-affine positive sharp QC remain OPEN.

cards.comparator: Classical null-Lagrangians, Fenchel/direct method and rank-one convexity; two-sided isotropic and degree-one-root transfers fail their hypotheses. Existing finite-H completion may change the coefficient.

cards.title: Autonomous quantum memory: exact structured-rate and persistent-bath interfaces
cards.scientific_scope: Internally reconstructed asynchronous 4D toric sweep; completed CPTP correctors, exact code initialization, one fixed perfect decoder, independent sparse Poisson locations.
cards.statement: Conditional on the universal location-only simultaneous Pauli-history certificate, arbitrary supported CPTP faults sharing a finite persistent bath factorize as Id_L tensor Lambda_B on every good schedule, including joint entangled inputs, and give joint-input diamond error <= 2 p_bad. For the specified signed GKSL catalog, CPTP uniformization is exact iff D is PSD, a lies in range(D), and r >= Gamma + tr(C) + a^* D^+ a, where D^+ is its Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse. For diagonal Pauli floors, with the stated zero-rate range convention, the exact minimum is sum_i gamma_i + sum_i h_i^2/gamma_i. Within the modewise floor/proposal family, common-cap spatial box and single-global-ellipsoid optima are 2 max_c sum_(i in S_c) epsilon_i and 2 max_c sqrt(sum_(i in S_c) b_i^2), respectively.
